questions.ask: What are the last four digits of your account number?

intents.hardship: The customer mentions financial hardship: job loss, illness, bereavement, being unable to afford essentials.
intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this product".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan, a restructuring or lower instalments.
intents.vague: A vague time with no exact date, e.g. "soon", "after payday".
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.
intents.human: A request to speak to a human.

lines.opening: Good day, this is Isla, Corran Bank's automated assistant. We record this call.
lines.robot: Yes, I am an automated assistant.
lines.scam: If you have any doubts, please call the number on the back of your card to check.
lines.purpose_before_verify: I can explain once I have confirmed I am speaking with the right person.
lines.no_info: I'm sorry, I can't share that information.
lines.not_talk_once: I understand. This will only take a few minutes.
lines.tp_ask: When would be a good time to call {first_name} back?
lines.tp_outside_window: I'm sorry, I can only call back on a business day, today or in the next two business days, between half past nine in the morning and six in the evening. Could you suggest another time?
lines.tp_no_info: I'm sorry, I can only discuss this with {first_name} {last_name}.
lines.tp_booked: Thank you. I will call back on {date} at {time}.
lines.wrong_number: I'm sorry for the trouble. Thank you for letting me know.
lines.condolence: I am very sorry for your loss.
lines.id_intro: Before we go on, I need to ask you two security questions.
lines.id_explain: I ask them to make sure I am speaking with the right person and to protect your account.
lines.id_declined: I understand. Without those answers I can't continue this call.
lines.id_repeat: Could you say that again, please?
lines.id_wrong: I'm sorry, that doesn't match the details I have.
lines.id_failed: I'm sorry, I can't confirm your identity. Please call the number on the back of your card or visit a branch.
lines.disclose_intro: Thank you. I'm calling about a late payment.
lines.product_line: Your {name} has {amount} past due, and it is {days} days late.
lines.ask_today: Can you pay the full amount today?
lines.ask_today_multi: Can you pay the full amount today?
lines.offer_floor_date: I understand. Could you pay {amount} on {date}?
lines.below_floor: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {floor}. Could you pay {floor}?
lines.below_floor_again: I'm sorry, that is still below the lowest amount I can accept.
lines.date_past: I'm sorry, the date must be today or later. Which date would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: I'm sorry, that day is not a business day. Could you pay on {date}?
lines.after_deadline: The latest date I can record is {date}. Could you pay by {date}?
lines.vague_ask: Could you give me an exact date?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?
lines.clamped_note: For your {name}, the latest date I can accept is {date}.
lines.sms_line: You will receive a confirmation by text message.
lines.record_failed: I'm sorry, your promise could not be recorded because of a system problem.
lines.paid_line: Thank you for letting me know. Payments can take two business days to show.
lines.dispute_line: I understand. I won't take a payment promise today.
lines.hardship: I'm very sorry to hear that. I'll transfer you to our care team, who can help.
lines.restructure_line: I'll transfer you to a colleague who can help with that.
lines.human_ask_help: Is there anything I can help you with first?
lines.transfer: I'm transferring you now. Please hold.
lines.anything_else: Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.promise_change: I'm sorry, I can't change the promise on this call.
lines.goodbye: Thank you for your time. Goodbye.
lines.callback_failed: I'm sorry, I couldn't book the callback.
lines.transfer_failed: I'm sorry, the transfer did not go through.
lines.confirm_again: Sorry, I did not catch that. Is that correct, yes or no?
lines.system_error: I'm sorry, our system is not responding right now.
lines.below_floor_final: I'm sorry, I can't record less than {amount}.

assumptions: Rule 1 gives the opening line as 'This call is recorded.' The spec format requires active voice and keeps the word 'recorded' for promise lines only, so the opening says 'We record this call.' instead. The rest of the prescribed opening is kept word for word.
Currency is pounds. The API says get_account amounts are in pounds, so amount_scale is 1. create_promise wants a whole number of pence (rule 32), so promise_scale is 100.

Floor (rule 22): minimum_due for credit cards and overdrafts, monthly_instalment for personal loans. If that value is higher than past_due, the floor is past_due, so floor = min(field, past_due). The brief gives no rounding, so floor amounts are used as given, pence included. Every floor offer uses this clamped floor.

Callback (rule 5): a business day that is today or one of the next two business days, from 09:30 to 18:00 with both ends included, and later than now. So days are today plus within_business_days:2, with business_days_only true. Rule 6 allows one more ask after a bad slot, so max_asks is 2. If both slots are outside the window, nothing is booked and the event is no_callback.
Confirm (rule 2): ask once more if the answer is unclear, so max_asks is 2.

Identity: postcode first, then account_last4 (rule 9). The postcode is sent in capitals with every space removed, so it has no format; it has no fixed length because postcode lengths vary. account_last4 is exactly 4 digits, leading zeros kept. Two wrong answers in total end the check (rule 11 and the API summary), so max_wrong is 2.

The verify_identity response has no hint field (its fields are ok, error, verified, wrong_answers_left, all_verified). So identity.response.hint is empty and hints is empty. No dates are asked, so date_order stays at the default dmy.

Rule 12: if the customer won't answer, the agent explains once that the questions protect the account. A second refusal is id_declined. The brief doesn't say whether asking what the call is about counts as declining, so the default (true) is kept.
date_rules.next_weekday: the brief says nothing, so the default following_week is used.
Early band deadline: the 8th business day after today, today not counted (rule 17).

Middle band deadline: today plus 14 calendar days, moved forward to the next business day if that date is not a business day (rule 18). That is why the global deadline_adjust is next_business_day. The early and late band rules always give a business day, so the forward adjust only affects the middle band.

Late band deadline (rule 19): the last business day of the current month, found by moving back from the last calendar day, so last_business_day_of_month is used. The brief rolls to next month's last business day only when this month's is EARLIER than today. A deadline equal to today stays, so roll_if_not_after_today is false. The engine is assumed to use next month's last business day if this month's is already past, which can only happen on a call made on a non-business day at the end of the month.
first_ask is today: 'Can you pay the full amount today?' (rule 25). It is not a proposal and uses no attempt, so the ladder's attempt 1 is the first proposal after the first flat refusal.

Ladders per band (rule 26). Attempt 1, all bands: past_due on the first business day after today, or on the deadline if that is earlier; the engine clamps proposal dates to the deadline. Attempt 2: the floor on the deadline (middle band) or past_due on the deadline (late band). Attempt 3, late band only: the floor on the deadline. Attempts allowed: early 1, middle 2, late 3.

Rule 24: if the customer says the full amount is too much, the floor is offered once on the date of the current proposal and uses no attempt, so too_much_floor is asked_date. From then on proposals use the floor instead of past_due, so the past_due steps are full_or_floor.

Rule 27: a step that would repeat an earlier amount and date exactly is skipped. It is not a proposal and the customer is not asked again. Example: in the late band after 'too much', attempt 2 (floor on the deadline) and attempt 3 (floor on the deadline) are identical, so attempt 3 is skipped. Likewise, if attempt 1 lands on the deadline, late-band attempt 2 (past_due on the deadline) is skipped.

Rule 20: for a non-business day, offer the next business day, or the deadline if that is earlier. The not_business_day line does not call {date} 'the next business day', because it may be the deadline. For a date after the deadline, say the deadline is the latest date and offer it. Rule 21: one ask for an exact date after a vague answer; a second vague answer is a flat refusal.
Below the floor (rule 24): say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. Refusing the floor is a flat refusal.
Hardship (rule 37): one sentence of sympathy, no further proposal, then transfer to the care queue without asking first. There is no add_note, because the table gives no note reason for transfers.
Notes are enabled: add_note with the product_id just before close_call, only for already paid (claims_paid), refused (customer_refused), dispute (disputed) and system failure (system_failure).
Rule 33: create_promise is retried once if it fails. A second failure is a system failure (no_promise / system_error, note system_failure).

The brief doesn't say how often 'I don't want to talk' is allowed, whether to ask 'anything else' after a promise, or how to change a recorded promise. Defaults are used: max_not_talk 2, ask_anything_else true, and the agent says the promise can't be changed on this call.

get_account returns a single 'product' object, not a list, so list_field is product, id_field is product_id and type_field is type. This is a one-product brief, so the multi settings keep their defaults and have no effect.
Rule 40: for a scam question, tell the customer to call the number on the back of their card, then continue. Rule 3: say yes to being an automated assistant and continue.
The close_call reason is left out for promise_made and already_paid ('none' in the table).
